finding: A whole-plan next route returned a mandatory batch playbook with state repair-required and command node atm.mjs batch repair --actor <id> --json. The commanded repair then failed with ATM_BATCH_RUN_MISSING, while node atm.mjs batch status --json reported no active batch and internally consistent state.
expectedBehavior: A returned recovery command must be executable against the state that produced it. If no active batch exists, next must either create or name a batch run before prescribing repair, or return a non-batch wait/claim route with the actual dependency blocker.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-09: node atm.mjs next --prompt "Continue all Plan 3.x/4.x task cards" --json returned channel=batch, state=repair-required, repairCommand=node atm.mjs batch repair --actor <id> --json. Running node atm.mjs batch repair --actor codex-gpt-5.4-mini --json failed ATM_BATCH_RUN_MISSING. node atm.mjs batch status --json then reported active=false, activeBatchCount=0, consistency.ok=true.
followUp: Add a regression that exercises the whole-plan route when the queue head is foreign-claimed and no batch run exists. Make the playbook select one reachable command, preserve the foreign-claim wait condition, and reject no-op repair advice. Keep batch repair strict once a real batch id exists.
